name: Justin
subhead: Strength, physique and bodybuilding competition prep.
introHeading: Give your effort a clear direction.

reasons.title: A goal worth working toward
reasons.text: Build muscle, develop your physique, or work toward a bodybuilding competition. Make the goal specific enough to guide your training.

reasons.title: A closer look at your training
reasons.text: Bring your training history, what is going well, and where you feel stuck.

reasons.title: A next step you understand
reasons.text: Discuss what coaching would involve and whether it fits the way you want to train.

faqs.question: Do I need to be an experienced lifter?
faqs.answer: Tell me where you are starting. Your experience, goals, and questions will help shape the conversation.

faqs.question: Can we talk about bodybuilding competition prep?
faqs.answer: Yes. Bring your training experience, the competition you’re considering, and any timeline you have. We’ll discuss your starting point and what prep would involve.

faqs.question: What does coaching include?
faqs.answer: Use the call to discuss the coaching options, support, and cost before deciding whether to begin.

closingHeading: Let’s see how strong you can get.
closingText: Start with your goal. We’ll take the conversation from there.

name: Zach
subhead: Strength coaching and tactical training, built around your goals.
introHeading: You don’t need every answer before you start.

reasons.title: Make your goal specific
reasons.text: Tell me whether you want strength coaching, tactical training, or to learn more about either.

reasons.title: Ask the questions you have
reasons.text: Bring your experience, uncertainties, and the skills you want to develop.

reasons.title: Understand the next step
reasons.text: Discuss the relevant training options and what working together would involve.

faqs.question: Can I ask about strength coaching or tactical training?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell me which area interests you so our conversation stays focused on what you need.

faqs.question: What if I’m new to training?
faqs.answer: Start with your experience and your questions. You do not need to know all the terminology to explain what you want to learn.

faqs.question: Do I need to choose a program before the call?
faqs.answer: No. Use the conversation to discuss your goal, the available options, and their costs before choosing a next step.

closingText: Bring your goals and your questions. Let’s work out where to start.

name: Rhylie
subhead: Strength, physique and bodybuilding competition prep for women.
introHeading: Your goal deserves a clear next step.

reasons.title: Make it your goal
reasons.text: Your goal might be getting stronger, building muscle, or bodybuilding competition prep. Talk about the progress that matters to you.

reasons.title: Start from your real life
reasons.text: Bring your training experience, available time, and what has made consistency difficult.

reasons.title: Know what progress means to you
reasons.text: Discuss the milestones and coaching support that would help you move forward.

faqs.question: Do I need to feel confident in the gym already?
faqs.answer: No. Share your starting point and what you want help understanding. That is useful information for the conversation.

faqs.question: Can I ask about bodybuilding competition prep?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tell me about your training experience, the competition you have in mind, and your timeline. We can discuss what prep would involve and where to start.

faqs.question: What if I’m unsure what coaching would involve?
faqs.answer: That is a good reason to talk. Use the call to discuss the options, support, and cost before deciding whether to begin.

closingHeading: Let’s build something you feel good about.
closingText: Start with what you want for yourself. We’ll talk about the next step.
